tests.title: Combined keeps Transaction and Cycle source boundaries aligned after column resize

tests.title: applies Inspector drafts, exposes Problems/JSON, and toggles panels

tests.title: edits Header and Footer metadata through Document Properties and reopens it

tests.title: Document Properties keeps Header and Legend edits in one Apply/Cancel transaction

tests.title: filters the Signal/Group tree by display name, path, role, or group without mutating the document

tests.title: Ctrl+D duplicates the selected Signal as one canonical command with a fresh stable ID
tests.primaryContract: Ctrl+D duplicates the selected Signal through the command route and produces exactly one new unique stable Signal identity without depending on rendered row count.
tests.reason: This is a single keyboard-to-semantic-command path with stable-ID uniqueness assertions; its identity contract is not established by testing the command handler alone.

tests.title: Ctrl+A selects every Signal without mutating the document
tests.primaryContract: Ctrl+A selects the current Signals without changing canonical revision or History.
tests.reason: The browser-level shortcut routing boundary and view-only state guarantee are concise and distinct from text-input native select-all behavior.

tests.title: Ctrl+A inside a text input performs native select-all instead of the app shortcut
tests.primaryContract: Ctrl+A in an available Signal name input performs native text selection and does not select the Signal collection; the test requires the editor input instead of silently skipping the contract.
tests.reason: A native editable control is the exception boundary for the global shortcut. Requiring the field prevents a missing Inspector control from making the test pass without checking the behavior.

tests.title: Escape cancels an in-progress Annotation drag, closes the context menu, and resets dependency-arrow pick
tests.primaryContract: Escape cancels a live Annotation drag without Canonical/History changes and clears dependent transient interaction state so later menu or Dependency gestures cannot inherit stale interaction state.
tests.reason: This combines pointer cancellation with context-menu and two-click Dependency state cleanup, so it is a multi-owner interaction lifecycle better suited to integration than routine PR coverage.

tests.title: Bottom tabs support keyboard roving focus and correct tabpanel semantics
tests.primaryContract: Keyboard users can move between Bottom tabs with arrow and End keys; focus, selected-tab state, and the labelled tabpanel stay synchronized without changing the document.
tests.reason: Accessible keyboard navigation and ARIA panel ownership are observable user contracts that pure state tests cannot establish in the rendered application. This is a compact one-page journey and distinct from pointer-based Bottom tab coverage.

tests.title: Focusable separators resize by keyboard within bounds without canonical mutation
tests.primaryContract: All four focusable pane separators respond to their orientation-specific keyboard controls, stop at declared minimum/maximum values, and leave Canonical revision, History, and Dirty unchanged.
tests.reason: This exercises four distinct production splitter owners and both boundaries through real keyboard events; the repeated extreme-boundary navigation is intentionally not part of the routine PR profile. Existing #722 discoverability/reset tests cover pointer affordance and double-click defaults, not keyboard resizing at both limits.

tests.title: keeps LabelAnchor source/display semantics on no-fold and folded ruler paths
tests.primaryContract: A standalone LabelAnchor rebases the visible ruler from source cycle 5 to display label 1000 both with and without a folded TimeGroup; Undo removes only the fold, and Save/Open preserves the canonical source/display pair.
tests.reason: This single cross-owner journey covers parsed canonical source/display data, no-fold and folded ruler projection, Undo, and a real Save/Open round trip. DOM attributes are used to expose the semantic source/display mapping while the rendered ruler text is also asserted; command tests provide the cheaper validation/lifecycle layer but cannot prove the shared projection path.

tests.title: edits global row layout through one semantic operation and preserves it through Save/Open
tests.primaryContract: Applying global row/label layout creates one semantic history operation, supports Undo/Redo, and Save/Open restores persisted layout settings.
tests.reason: This covers a genuine Save/Open persistence lifecycle after editing multiple layout fields; it should not run in the small routine PR cohort.

tests.title: cancels layout draft without a canonical mutation
tests.primaryContract: Canceling an edited layout draft leaves Canonical revision and History unchanged.
tests.reason: This isolates a low-cost Draft/Cancel semantic boundary and complements the heavier Apply/Save/Open journey.

tests.title: auto fits a long rendered signal label through one layout command
tests.primaryContract: Auto Fit proposes a width in the layout draft, Apply commits it once, and Undo restores the prior width.
tests.reason: A long-name production journey checks both a presentation-derived suggestion and command/Undo semantics; retain as one focused integration example rather than cloning it across multiple label styles.

tests.title: renders persisted label columns independently from the transient pane splitter
tests.primaryContract: Applying persisted label widths/alignment/overflow updates the rendered columns independently from the transient splitter, and Reset restores defaults.
tests.reason: It asserts internal CSS grid templates, whitespace, and render counters; retain the layout contract in visual tier while decoupling from incidental DOM/CSS details.

tests.title: right-aligns Left Tree header actions without changing command behavior
tests.primaryContract: Left Tree header title and Add/More controls remain aligned and usable at minimum, normal, and maximum pane widths; Add/More menus still open and resizing remains view-only.
tests.reason: The contract is explicitly pixel/layout-sensitive, relies on rendered element bounds and fixed gap tolerances, and takes 10.6s; keep this single case in the visual profile. It complements icon-asset and responsive-pane checks by protecting control alignment through actual Add/More use and resizing, rather than repeating those contracts.

tests.title: left pane starts at the approved minimum without a resize jump (/?visual-reference)
tests.primaryContract: On the visual-reference route at 1672x941, the left-pane separator starts at the approved 265px minimum, exposes the 265–420px bounds, and neither an outward keyboard press nor pointer drag shrinks it below minimum.
tests.reason: This protects the visual-reference route's Cycle-oriented fixture/initial owner; its measured runtime is below 10s. The normal-route counterpart starts from a different document/workspace path, so retain both route contracts rather than dropping one as a duplicate.

tests.title: left pane starts at the approved minimum without a resize jump (/)
tests.primaryContract: On the normal product route at 1672x941, the left-pane separator starts at the approved 265px minimum, exposes the 265–420px bounds, and neither an outward keyboard press nor pointer drag shrinks it below minimum.
tests.reason: This protects the normal route's default Transaction-document startup followed by Cycle initialization; its measured runtime is below 10s. The reference-route counterpart has a different initial document/workspace owner and is retained separately.

tests.title: Left Tree header actions use owned SVG icons without changing the document
tests.primaryContract: From the production Cycle Tree header, users can open/close More and Add menus with focus restored on Escape, expand groups, and clear a filter without changing document/history/dirty state.
tests.reason: Keep the user-visible menu/focus and view-only behavior, but move exact SVG child counts, pseudo-element text, and renderer-counter equality into component/architecture-level coverage. left-tree-critical-icons.spec.ts already owns cross-fixture SVG topology; this E2E should not couple user behavior to those DOM internals.
tests.replacementTest: Retain a focused user-journey E2E for accessible Add/More, Escape focus restoration, Expand All, filter clear, and canonical/history/dirty invariance; cover owned SVG markup and render-counter invalidation in component/architecture tests.

tests.title: keeps the left tree footer compact at laptop viewport
tests.primaryContract: At 1280x720, the Cycle Left Tree footer remains compact without horizontal overflow or redundant hierarchy UI, while Add/More entry points work without document mutation.
tests.reason: This checks a real compact viewport boundary plus footer content and action discoverability; its 9.7s focused runtime belongs in visual acceptance rather than routine PR. The larger viewport case is retained separately for its distinct supported viewport contract.

tests.title: keeps the left tree footer compact at the Golden viewport
tests.primaryContract: At 1672x941, the Cycle Left Tree footer remains compact without horizontal overflow or redundant hierarchy UI, while Add/More entry points work without document mutation.
tests.reason: This protects the reference-sized production viewport; the laptop counterpart is also retained because responsive width can change wrapping/overflow and both measured runs are short enough for the visual profile.

tests.title: Left Tree critical icons are inline SVG and identical across production fixtures
tests.primaryContract: Visibility, row More, and group-collapse icons render with owned SVG geometry consistently in the normal and visual-reference Cycle fixtures.
tests.reason: This is a cross-fixture rendering contract for the core navigation icons, distinct from Add/More header actions and from user menu behavior. Its SVG topology selectors are implementation-coupled, so keep it out of routine PR and prefer moving the invariant to component tests when such coverage exists.

tests.title: collapses only Left Tree descendants and restores stable rows without a canonical mutation
tests.primaryContract: Collapsing a Left Tree group hides only its navigation descendants, preserves frozen/timing rows and wave owners, and restores the exact stable row order without changing Canonical or History.
tests.reason: This guards separation between navigation disclosure and timing projection across three groups and exact row restoration; the DOM projection assertions are appropriate as an integration owner contract rather than routine user smoke.

tests.title: visibility keeps the navigation row but removes and restores derived signal surfaces
tests.primaryContract: Toggling Signal visibility keeps its navigation row while removing and restoring frozen/timing rows and the Wave owner for the same stable signal ID.
tests.reason: This isolates visibility projection from group collapse: the same stable signal identity remains navigable while only its derived presentation surfaces change. It complements collapse coverage without duplicating it.

tests.title: row and group More commands route to the shared context menu and insertion follows selection
tests.primaryContract: Row and group More affordances open the supported shared menus, and adding a Signal after selecting a row inserts it at the expected stable position after a group reorder.
tests.reason: This verifies a compound production journey across context menus, group ordering, selection, and semantic insertion placement; it is distinct from header menu affordance and simpler command-unit coverage.

tests.title: Left Tree menus keep readable normal, hover, focus, and disabled states
tests.primaryContract: Left Tree More and row context menus retain readable normal/hover/disabled colors, visible keyboard focus and arrow navigation, Escape dismissal, and no document mutation.
tests.reason: Computed color assertions are theme/visual acceptance, while focus traversal and Escape dismissal cover keyboard accessibility not guaranteed by the menu-open/focus-return checks in other tests. Keep this combined state matrix outside routine PR runs.

tests.title: Group Collapse owns only Left Tree disclosure and compacts following tree groups
tests.primaryContract: Collapsing a group compacts Left Tree descendants while preserving Cycle frozen/timing/wave surfaces and stable row order without document/history/dirty or expensive geometry/render work.
tests.reason: The case measures relative positions and owner counters across tree and Cycle projections, which provides geometry/invalidation evidence beyond the compact collapse-and-restore user flow; retain as the integration-level projection contract.

tests.title: Signal Visibility owns timing presentation independently from collapsed tree disclosure
tests.primaryContract: A hidden Signal remains hidden when its Left Tree group is collapsed, and applying visibility from Inspector restores Cycle surfaces without implicitly expanding the tree; disclosure and visibility stay independent.
tests.reason: This covers the cross-owner edge case where Inspector changes visibility while the navigation group is collapsed; the simpler visible-row toggle contract does not prove that disclosure remains independent.

tests.title: combines the Left Tree type and text filters without mutation at 1000px
tests.primaryContract: At 1000px, combining type and text filters shows only matching Left Tree rows, leaves timing/frozen/wave surfaces intact, and does not change Canonical, History, Dirty, or render counters.
tests.reason: This independently validates compact-width availability and view-only semantics under the same type/text filtering journey; it protects a separate supported viewport boundary rather than duplicating the 1672px contract.

tests.title: combines the Left Tree type and text filters without mutation at 1672px
tests.primaryContract: At 1672px, combining type and text filters shows only matching Left Tree rows, leaves timing/frozen/wave surfaces intact, and does not change Canonical, History, Dirty, or render counters.
tests.reason: This validates the normal supported-width user flow across Input/Output/Wire/Comment filters, text matching, and no-mutation behavior. The compact-width counterpart remains necessary for responsive layout/filter coexistence.

tests.title: registers the Left Tree keydown handler exactly once per mount (no duplicate listener)
tests.primaryContract: A Cycle Tree mount does not accumulate keydown registrations on the Left Tree rows element, including React StrictMode's development remount behavior.
tests.reason: The test instruments the native listener registration boundary to guard against duplicate keyboard handlers; the following ArrowDown behavior test checks the user-visible consequence but cannot reliably detect duplicated registration when effects remount.

tests.title: one ArrowDown moves Left Tree keyboard focus by exactly one row, not two
tests.primaryContract: One ArrowDown press advances Left Tree row focus by exactly one stable row, preserving expected keyboard navigation behavior.
tests.reason: This is a concise externally observable keyboard-navigation assertion; it complements the listener lifecycle guard with a direct focus outcome and is cheap enough for the focused PR browser tier.

tests.title: keeps WaveDrom DOM writes and Local Geometry reads inside one render batch
tests.primaryContract: A clean Cycle startup batches all WaveDrom owners under one render batch and performs one Local Geometry build per owner, without changing History or Dirty state.
tests.reason: The test checks a renderer/geometry batching invariant and exact owner counters; it provides focused architecture/performance evidence and should not be treated as broad correctness or ordinary PR acceptance.

tests.title: drags the Measurement start anchor independently -- only that endpoint moves, preview is transient, drop is one History unit
tests.primaryContract: Dragging a Measurement start handle previews without Canonical/History changes, commits only the start endpoint in one History unit, and does not rebuild unrelated WaveDrom or Local Geometry owners.
tests.reason: This is the full start-endpoint geometry/preview/commit boundary, including incremental-render invariants; the opposite endpoint has a separate direction-specific case, while cheaper command tests cannot validate pointer projection.

tests.title: drags the Measurement end anchor independently -- only that endpoint moves
tests.primaryContract: Dragging a Measurement end handle changes that endpoint only and produces exactly one History unit, leaving the start anchor unchanged.
tests.reason: End-edge projection can diverge from start-edge behavior and is not implied by the start-handle case; retain this direction-specific acceptance until both handles are exercised by one parameterized test with equivalent assertions.

tests.title: Escape mid-drag cancels the Measurement anchor drag and returns exactly to the pre-drag state
tests.primaryContract: Pressing Escape during an active Measurement handle drag cancels preview and restores the exact pre-drag Canonical and History state.
tests.reason: This is a concise cancellation journey at the active-pointer lifecycle boundary; Undo/Redo tests cover committed edits, not Escape before commit.

tests.title: Undo restores the pre-drag anchor exactly, Redo re-applies it, and Save/Open preserves the moved anchor
tests.primaryContract: A moved Measurement anchor is one reversible semantic edit and its resulting annotation geometry survives an actual Save/New/Open round trip.
tests.reason: Combines pointer geometry, exact Undo/Redo restoration, file download, document replacement, and Open; keep as a heavy persistence lifecycle rather than routine PR validation.

tests.title: same-Signal Measurement: geometry survives Zoom 50/100/150/200%, horizontal scroll, and Signal reorder
tests.primaryContract: The same stable Measurement anchors remain semantically resolved across 50/100/150/200% zoom, horizontal scroll, and Signal reorder.
tests.reason: This covers shared geometry rebinding across multiple view transforms and a row reorder, distinct from endpoint drag or persistence. It reads semantic aria labels rather than requiring screen pixels to remain fixed; the direct scroll mutation and fixed wait should be replaced with observable scroll completion when this test is next touched.

tests.title: Measurement start/end markers, arrow layout and extension lines have real rendered effect, one History unit per Apply, and survive Undo/Redo + Save/Open
tests.primaryContract: Measurement marker kinds, arrow direction, and extension-line sides visibly affect production projection, apply as one History unit, restore through Undo/Redo, and persist through Save/Open.
tests.reason: This is a full semantic-to-rendered layout and persistence lifecycle spanning four editor fields and actual file I/O; retain as heavy acceptance, not routine PR verification.

tests.title: exports overlapping same-Signal Measurements with inward and outward arrow layouts, partial extension lines, and correct lane stacking
tests.primaryContract: SVG export preserves marker kinds, inward/outward arrow layout, per-side extension lines, stable Annotation IDs, and distinct auto-stacked lanes for overlapping same-Signal Measurements.
tests.reason: This combines two overlapping authored Measurements, multiple layout configurations, and downloaded SVG inspection. Cross-Signal ratio and the simpler auto-lane algorithm have separate tests; keep this remaining same-Signal export combination in the heavy lifecycle tier.

tests.title: two overlapping Measurements with no explicit lane auto-stack onto different lanes
tests.primaryContract: Two fully overlapping Measurements without explicit lanes are assigned different automatic lanes rather than both remaining on lane 0.
tests.reason: This is the base collision-packing invariant; the three-Measurement test below covers exhaustion of both existing lanes, which is a distinct allocator boundary.

tests.title: a third Measurement overlapping both stacks onto lane 2, not back onto lane 0 or 1
tests.primaryContract: A third Measurement overlapping both existing stacks is placed on a new lane 2 rather than reusing either occupied lane.
tests.reason: This tests the allocator's next-free-lane behavior after both current lanes are occupied and cannot be inferred from the pairwise overlap case.

tests.title: renders and exports a cross-Signal ratio Measurement through the production browser path
tests.primaryContract: A file-opened cross-Signal ratio Measurement resolves both ratio anchors in production projection and retains ratio anchor semantics in exported SVG.
tests.reason: This specifically spans two stable Signal IDs, ratio-based endpoints, production document loading, and export. Same-Signal visual/lane tests do not exercise cross-Signal anchor resolution.

tests.title: a Measurement anchored on the top-row Signal places its label/line below the row, never behind the Ruler
tests.primaryContract: A Measurement anchored to the first Signal chooses below-row placement so its label, body, and markers do not overlap the Cycle Ruler.
tests.reason: This checks real rendered bounding-box non-overlap at the ruler boundary, a distinct visual clipping condition not covered by semantic layout command tests.

tests.title: a Measurement anchored well below the top row keeps its default above-the-line placement
tests.primaryContract: A Measurement on a row with sufficient clearance retains the default above-the-line side instead of applying the top-row fallback globally.
tests.reason: This is the positive counterpart to the top-row fallback: it prevents a broad below-row placement policy from regressing Measurements with normal clearance.

tests.title: browser diagnostics detect injected clipping, overlap, duplication, and icon drift
tests.primaryContract: The mechanical visual analyzer recognizes four deliberately injected diagnostic categories and reports major findings with evidence.
tests.reason: The case uses page.setContent and an in-memory synthetic DOM only; tests/harness/mechanical-diagnostics.test.ts already exercises the same negative categories directly at the harness unit layer, making this E2E wrapper duplicate coverage without testing the production app.

tests.title: projects canonical rows into aligned tree, frozen labels, and waveform surfaces
tests.primaryContract: The same canonical Signal ID order projects into Left Tree, frozen labels, semantic timing rows, and one waveform per Signal with consistent row Y positions and group markers.
tests.reason: This is the foundational multi-surface row identity/alignment contract; tests for individual visibility/collapse behaviors do not prove the complete canonical-to-wave projection order.

tests.title: derives the ruler from local geometry and keeps selection view-only
tests.primaryContract: Ruler ticks come from local geometry in strictly increasing unique positions, while selecting a Signal propagates stable selection across surfaces without rebuilding geometry or changing document/history.
tests.reason: This joins the ruler geometry owner and cross-surface selection projection invariants without asserting fixed pixel positions; it is distinct from drag and viewport lifecycle cases.

tests.title: synchronizes scrolling through one viewport without regenerating waveforms
tests.primaryContract: One Cycle viewport scroll owner synchronizes horizontal and vertical position while retaining WaveDrom DOM identities, avoiding full row scans/RowLayout rebuilds, and keeping frozen labels aligned.
tests.reason: This protects a shared viewport owner and incremental projection contract across both scroll axes. Exact internal counters and direct scroll assignment make it an integration/architecture check; replace synthetic scroll mutation with a real interaction when the test is next updated.

tests.title: MiniMap viewport updates do not rebuild the static overview
tests.primaryContract: Viewport scrolling and MiniMap pan reuse the static overview rows/lookups and do not change document, History, Dirty, validation, waveform, or geometry state.
tests.reason: This measures overview cache reuse under viewport-only operations with explicit semantic and render no-change checks; its cache counters are architectural evidence and should stay outside generic user-journey PR smoke.

tests.title: non-overview Signal property commits reuse the static MiniMap overview
tests.primaryContract: Committing a Signal rename updates canonical data/history/dirty state without rebuilding the static MiniMap overview when the changed property does not affect its projection.
tests.reason: This covers invalidation precision after a real semantic commit, complementary to the viewport-only case; the pair distinguishes correct reuse from simply never rebuilding the overview.

tests.title: MiniMap viewport indicator follows live scroll, resize, pan and remount state
tests.primaryContract: At 1280x720 the MiniMap viewport rectangle tracks vertical/horizontal scrolling, resize, real pointer panning, zoom, and hide/remount state within normalized geometry bounds without document mutation.
tests.reason: This is a multi-axis geometry and lifecycle acceptance journey with real pointer pan, resize, zoom, and remount; keep it as heavy integration rather than repeat it in ordinary PR runs.

tests.title: Cycle/Transaction/Combined presentation state stays isolated at 1280x720
tests.primaryContract: At 1280x720, Cycle, Transaction, and Combined preserve their own selection, zoom, pane sizing/visibility, scroll, split ratio, and independent vertical positions across repeated mode switches without document mutation.
tests.reason: This exercises a large production-opened document through repeated mode switches and many independent presentation controls at the compact viewport; the larger viewport companion protects a distinct responsive boundary.

tests.title: Cycle/Transaction/Combined presentation state stays isolated at 1672x941
tests.primaryContract: At 1672x941, Cycle, Transaction, and Combined preserve their own selection, zoom, pane sizing/visibility, scroll, split ratio, and independent vertical positions across repeated mode switches without document mutation.
tests.reason: This is the reference-size companion to the compact viewport journey. Both share the same semantic state-isolation contract, but the independent viewport changes real overflow and pane geometry conditions and warrants separate heavy-tier evidence.

tests.title: same-named Signal selection cannot transfer an uncommitted rename
tests.primaryContract: An uncommitted Inspector rename draft remains scoped to its stable Signal identity; switching between same-named Signals cannot transfer the draft or create an unintended History entry.
tests.reason: This guards against name-based identity collisions across selection changes with both entities first given the same name, a stronger adversarial case than switching between differently named Signals. It remains useful after #208's separate Transaction hit-target fix.

tests.title: drops WaveDrom results that belong to a replaced document epoch
tests.primaryContract: Opening a second document during the first document's bounded WaveDrom batch drops stale results from the replaced document epoch and leaves only the new document's rows/owners.
tests.reason: This deterministically forces an Open race while rendering a 500-signal document and asserts stale-owner rejection at document replacement; it guards an asynchronous identity boundary not covered by final-document smoke tests.

tests.title: yields between bounded WaveDrom batches during Open
tests.primaryContract: Opening a 100-signal/500-cycle document yields between bounded WaveDrom batches (maximum size 8), shows progress before idle, and finishes cleanly without document mutation.
tests.reason: This validates bounded batch sizing, frame yielding and progress observability with a large fixture and runtime counters; retain in the heavy performance gate, not routine focused browser runs.

tests.title: makes the reference ruler usable before all visible waves finish
tests.primaryContract: During progressive Open, a usable reference Cycle Ruler is rendered while WaveDrom batches are still pending, before the document reaches idle.
tests.reason: This protects first-usable-time behavior rather than eventual render completion: ruler ticks must be available during pending waveform work. It complements batch-yield accounting with an observable early interaction surface.

tests.title: hands a validated Open document to the new session without duplicate session validation
tests.primaryContract: The production Save -> file-input Open route hands the parser-trusted canonical document into a fresh session without a second validation or semantic commit, and resets History/Dirty exactly once.
tests.reason: Core unit coverage proves the DocumentSession accepts parser-trusted data without revalidation, but only this production file route verifies the GUI passes that trusted result through the replacement lifecycle and reports the correct session counters. Keep one integration boundary check; do not expand it into a large Open matrix.

tests.title: rejects an oversized Open file before reading and preserves document state
tests.primaryContract: A production Open request above MAX_OPEN_FILE_BYTES is rejected before File.text/parse and leaves the current canonical revision, History, Dirty state, and document title unchanged while surfacing a user-visible problem.
tests.reason: The actual browser File input route is required to prove the size guard precedes file reading and that diagnostics/state preservation reach the UI. Lower-level byte-budget logic can be unit-tested, but cannot replace this single production-boundary check; retain outside routine PR smoke because it allocates a >32 MB File.

tests.title: rejects an over-budget canonical resource before session replacement
tests.primaryContract: A syntactically valid Open document that exceeds the canonical cycle resource budget is rejected before replacing the active session; revision, History, Dirty state, and title remain unchanged and the user receives a resource-limit diagnostic.
tests.reason: This exercises parse/migrate/validate plus the GUI replacement boundary with a real file-input payload and checks the old document survives. Core unit tests cover commit-time resource rejection, not this Open route's user-visible diagnostic and no-replacement contract, so keep one bounded integration test.

tests.title: far jump long-task measurement (100 signals x 10000 cycles, Combined)
tests.primaryContract: A far horizontal viewport jump in Combined mode on a 100-signal/10,000-cycle document stays within the production main-thread long-task budget and does not fall back to per-cycle SVG WaveDrom nodes.
tests.reason: This is an intentionally large performance measurement with tracing, long-task observation, and a 1M signal-cycle document. Keep it in the dedicated performance/nightly tier; it is not a routine correctness or PR test and was not run during inventory review.

tests.title: View-only operations keep canonical validation and render counters unchanged
tests.primaryContract: Selection, panel, zoom, scroll, and explicit Refresh Checks leave document/history unchanged; passive operations avoid expensive validator/render work while Refresh Checks invokes validation once.
tests.reason: Separates semantic no-mutation behavior from internal cost counters; retain the expensive-owner invariant as integration/architecture evidence rather than a generic user journey.

tests.title: SnapIndex cache survives a non-geometric Signal rename
tests.primaryContract: Renaming a Signal does not rebuild the time-geometry SnapIndex because the edit is non-geometric.
tests.reason: This guards an owner/invalidation cost boundary using internal counters; keep it in a dedicated performance/architecture gate and add cheaper invalidation-policy unit coverage where available.

tests.title: retargets the SnapIndex after a vertical viewport jump
tests.primaryContract: A viewport jump retargets SnapIndex queries to newly visible rows without scanning every row and still resolves a bottom-row annotation endpoint.
tests.reason: Uses a 1k Signal document, vertical virtualization, pointer queries, and internal build/visit counters; retain in heavy performance validation, not PR.

tests.title: heavy renderer diagnostics are pull-based and absent from hot-path DOM counters
tests.primaryContract: Heavy per-signal diagnostic maps are absent from published hot-path attributes but remain available through an explicit pull snapshot API.
tests.reason: This is an internal observability/serialization architecture contract rather than user behavior; keep in the dedicated performance architecture gate and avoid general E2E duplication.

tests.title: PR guard: 100x500 selection/reorder/edit/annotation/view hard invariants with browser median/p95
tests.primaryContract: On the 100x500 representative fixture, user-visible interaction performance is sampled while selection/reorder/edit/annotation/view preserve documented render, geometry, History, and dirty-state invariants.
tests.reason: The test explicitly defines a PR guard with a representative, not 10k+, fixture and reports median/p95; retain in PR pending measured runtime evidence, while replacing exact internal counters with user-cost budgets where possible.

tests.title: 1000x1000 virtualization mounts viewport-scale rows and avoids duplicate bindings
tests.primaryContract: A 1000x1000 document maintains viewport-scale mounted rows/owners and bounded caches through repeated vertical scrolling, with no duplicate stable Signal bindings.
tests.reason: Large synthetic document plus repeated scroll and owner/cache diagnostics is an intentional performance gate; preserve it outside the routine PR suite.

tests.title: large valid fixture records Open/Save browser profile evidence
tests.primaryContract: A valid 1000x1000 fixture can open and save while browser-level timing and resource evidence is recorded.
tests.reason: Large-document Open/Save is a high-cost persistence benchmark; retain as automated integration/performance evidence and do not run in ordinary focused PR verification.

tests.title: viewport-only projection remains bounded at 1k, 5k, and 10k rows
tests.primaryContract: For 1k/5k/10k Signal documents, viewport scrolling visits a bounded row set without full scans or RowLayout rebuilds.
tests.reason: This multi-size scaling sweep is explicit large-fixture performance coverage; keep it automated in performance/nightly rather than routine PR.

tests.title: repeated Open A/B/A releases old owners and does not stack handlers
tests.primaryContract: Repeated document replacement releases stale renderer/row owners and handlers, keeps caches bounded, and leaves the new active Signal editable.
tests.reason: Exercises repeated Open, forced GC, owner/cache diagnostics, and a final edit; preserve as automated nightly lifecycle coverage.

tests.title: Open first-correct-paint has median and p95 evidence across scale fixtures
tests.primaryContract: First correct render after Open has reported median/p95 measurements across small, representative, and long-cycle documents.
tests.reason: Runs repeated Opens across multiple fixtures to produce scale-specific timing distributions; this is a benchmark, not a correctness smoke.

tests.title: nightly/manual 500/1000 heavy profiles
tests.primaryContract: Nightly PERF_SCALE execution exercises annotation-heavy 500x500 and transaction-heavy 1000x1000 profiles and records renderer/DOM diagnostics.
tests.reason: This is the heaviest profile and was previously permanently skipped because test:perf:nightly did not set PERF_SCALE; the runner is being corrected to make the nightly path actually execute it.

tests.title: measures GUI latency inside Chromium rather than through Playwright RPC time
tests.primaryContract: Representative real GUI clicks and scrolls complete through the next browser animation frame under the declared responsiveness budget, measured in Chromium rather than Playwright RPC wall time.
tests.reason: The in-page capture distinguishes browser interaction/frame response from automation transport delay and samples selection, Ribbon, zoom, panel visibility, and scroll. This is performance evidence, not a replacement for semantic invariants; keep it in the performance profile rather than PR smoke.

tests.title: view-only GUI operations do not validate or semantically rerender the document
tests.primaryContract: Selection, Ribbon/Bottom tabs, zoom, workspace/density, panel visibility, pane resizing, and scrolling do not change Canonical/History/Dirty or trigger validation, WaveDrom rendering, local geometry, or RowLayout rebuilds.
tests.reason: This broader action set includes pane resizers and workspace/density state not present in performance-closure.spec.ts case 615. Case 615 separately verifies whole-document validatorInvocations remain unchanged and that explicit Refresh Checks increments exactly once; retain both because the counters/owners and protected invalidation boundaries differ.

tests.title: pinned Signal visibility and duplicate actions target the pinned stable ID
tests.primaryContract: With Bottom Pin active, visibility and Clock duplicate actions continue targeting the displayed stable Signal ID after global selection changes to another Signal.
tests.reason: This is the production regression for selection-relative Signal actions under Pin and covers two distinct command adapters (visibility and duplicate) against a changed live selection. Existing unit tests only cover pin snapshot capture, not the action target identity.

tests.title: pinned Annotation stays on the collection surface and deletes the created annotation
tests.primaryContract: Changing Signal selection while Bottom Pin retains the Annotation collection surface, and collection Delete removes exactly the created stable Annotation ID without affecting other annotations or the newly selected Signal.
tests.reason: Annotation collection lifetime and delete routing are distinct from Signal/Transaction action adapters; the test resolves and checks the created entity identity through the real GUI collection.

tests.title: pinned Signal delete targets the pinned stable ID
tests.primaryContract: After selection moves from the pinned Signal to another Signal, Bottom Delete removes the pinned stable ID, preserves the current selection target, creates one History operation, and clears the deleted pin safely.
tests.reason: Delete has separate mutation and post-delete selection/pin cleanup semantics from visibility/duplicate actions; retain one focused production route for that behavior.

tests.title: pinned Transaction edits target the pinned stable ID
tests.primaryContract: A pinned Transaction remains the Bottom/Inspector target across Combined mode and unrelated Signal selection, and Apply edits that Transaction's stable ID without mutating the Signal or another Transaction.
tests.reason: This crosses Transaction authoring, Bottom pin state, Combined mode, tree selection, and Inspector Apply; its route is materially different from the Signal and Annotation actions and cannot be proven by the pin-capture unit test.

tests.title: normal and visual-reference use one Production presentation contract
tests.primaryContract: At the reference viewport, normal and visual-reference routes expose the same production ribbon structure, tabs, pane geometry, and design tokens.
tests.reason: This compares separately booted production routes for architectural/presentation equivalence rather than against a golden image; source inspection or component tests cannot prove both routes resolve to identical live DOM geometry and computed tokens.

tests.title: Cycle, Transaction and Combined remain usable at 1280x720
tests.primaryContract: At the compact 1280x720 viewport, Cycle, Transaction, and Combined surfaces remain mounted/usable through mode switching without Canonical, History, Dirty, or session-counter changes.
tests.reason: The compact viewport has distinct responsive constraints and confirms all three mode surfaces and Combined controls remain available; preserve as a browser contract. Its screenshot is attached to Playwright output rather than written over a tracked artifact.

tests.title: Cycle, Transaction and Combined remain usable at 1672x941
tests.primaryContract: At the 1672x941 reference viewport, Cycle, Transaction, and Combined surfaces remain mounted/usable through mode switching without Canonical, History, Dirty, or session-counter changes.
tests.reason: This protects the reference-size layout independently of compact viewport overflow/clipping behavior. Both screenshots are retained as Playwright attachments, not tracked baseline edits.

tests.title: J1-3 fresh -> Combined: renders, view-only, no errors
tests.primaryContract: A fresh application can enter Combined mode without changing Canonical, History, or Dirty state and without runtime errors.
tests.reason: Combined composes two view owners and needs its own real startup journey; this is not covered by either single mode.

tests.title: J1-3 fresh -> Cycle: renders, view-only, no errors
tests.primaryContract: A fresh application can enter Cycle mode without changing Canonical, History, or Dirty state and without runtime errors.
tests.reason: Representative fresh-state Cycle entry journey; complementary Transaction and Combined entries are also retained in the same product lifecycle contract suite.

tests.title: J1-3 fresh -> Transaction: renders, view-only, no errors
tests.primaryContract: A fresh application can enter Transaction mode without changing Canonical, History, or Dirty state and without runtime errors.
tests.reason: Transaction workspace has a separate initialization/projection path, so this user-visible mode entry complements Cycle and Combined smoke journeys.

tests.title: J4/J16 Cycle -> Transaction -> Combined -> Cycle, then rapid switching, stays view-only and error-free
tests.primaryContract: Mode transitions and rapid switching preserve document/history state and keep the application error-free.
tests.reason: This is the direct cross-mode lifecycle invariant and exercises state transitions that static/unit tests cannot fully prove.

tests.title: J5/J10 select -> edit -> Apply -> Undo -> Redo, and an unapplied draft does not leak to the next selection
tests.primaryContract: Selection changes discard an unapplied draft; Apply creates one history step and Undo/Redo restore the committed state.
tests.reason: This production journey covers cross-selection draft isolation plus the visible Apply/Undo/Redo contract, which is not reducible to a single unit invariant.

tests.title: J7/J8/J15 far horizontal + vertical scroll -> select, zoom -> scroll -> mode switch
tests.primaryContract: A fresh Cycle workspace can scroll horizontally and vertically, select after the far scroll, zoom, reposition, and survive mode round trips without runtime errors.
tests.reason: This verifies a real fresh-start interaction sequence spanning both scroll axes, selection, zoom, and mode ownership; separate owner tests do not prove the combined lifecycle order.

tests.title: J9 Bottom follows the selected entity kind
tests.primaryContract: Bottom panel follows the selected entity kind across the actual application surface.
tests.reason: The selected entity kind drives a cross-surface panel contract that is appropriately verified at the UI boundary.

tests.title: J11-J14 save -> edit -> Undo, dirty -> Open -> Cancel / Discard, reload -> Open
tests.primaryContract: A fresh Cycle document can be saved, edited, undone/redone, protected by Cancel or replaced by Discard during Open, then reloaded and opened again without runtime errors.
tests.reason: Although focused tests cover individual dirty-dialog paths, this test uniquely verifies their end-to-end ordering with Save/download, edit history, browser reload, and a second Open in one fresh session.

tests.title: J17 window resize during an active range drag keeps the app consistent
tests.primaryContract: Resizing the browser viewport during a live Cycle range drag leaves the editor idle, creates no History unit, and produces no runtime errors.
tests.reason: This is the only reviewed live range-drag plus viewport-resize lifecycle; static geometry and ordinary range-drag tests do not cover resize during pointer capture.

tests.title: active Reference Clock conversion discloses and atomically enters clockless mode
tests.primaryContract: Converting the active Reference Clock presents the designation-loss consequence, Cancel is view-only, confirmation removes the designation without implicit replacement, and Undo/Redo restore the exact clockless/clock states.
tests.reason: The command unit test covers conversion planning but cannot prove the user-facing destructive-change disclosure, Cancel boundary, time-axis transition, or history lifecycle through the Inspector confirmation dialog.

tests.title: converts a Clock to binary with exact canonical defaults and Save/Open
tests.primaryContract: Inspector conversion to Binary preserves Signal identity and source, removes Clock-only properties/reference designation, assigns exact binary defaults, and those semantics survive Save/Open.
tests.reason: The real Inspector plus serialization path is not covered by the semantic conversion unit test; Binary's numeric initial value and Clock-only field removal are its target-specific data contract.

tests.title: converts a Clock to bus with exact canonical defaults and Save/Open
tests.primaryContract: Inspector conversion to Bus preserves identity/source, removes Clock-only properties/reference designation, sets width 8/hex format and the canonical initial bus value, and survives Save/Open.
tests.reason: Bus conversion has additional width/display-format defaults absent from Binary/State; it independently protects that variant through production Save/Open.

tests.title: converts a Clock to state with exact canonical defaults and Save/Open
tests.primaryContract: Inspector conversion to State preserves identity/source, removes Clock-only properties/reference designation, assigns the canonical IDLE initial value, and survives Save/Open.
tests.reason: State's symbolic IDLE default differs from Binary and Bus values; keeping this target-specific round trip detects conversion serializers that only handle numeric/value-signal variants.

tests.title: creates an empty Signal Group from the tree through one group.create command
tests.primaryContract: The Tree Add menu creates an empty Group in one History operation, selects it in the Group Inspector, and causes no WaveDrom/local-geometry rebuild; Undo removes it.
tests.reason: This protects the direct Left Tree Add adapter for creating an empty Group and its one-command/zero-render effects. The broader empty-group projection/persistence journey covers cross-surface lifecycle but not this exact Add-menu command boundary.

tests.title: Group Inspector reflects and controls view-only collapse state
tests.primaryContract: The Inspector's Group collapsed property tracks Tree disclosure and can collapse/expand that Group without Canonical/History mutation or waveform/geometry rebuild.
tests.reason: The other reviewed Group-collapse tests focus on Left Tree-only disclosure and projection separation; this specifically tests the Inspector adapter/state reflection and zero-invalidation behavior.

tests.title: hides and restores a selected signal without rebuilding its stable SVG
tests.primaryContract: Tree visibility removes/restores the selected Signal's derived surfaces while preserving its SVG node identity and avoiding WaveDrom/local-geometry rebuild; only row positions update.
tests.reason: left-tree-interaction.spec.ts verifies navigation-row retention and derived-surface presence, while this protects stable SVG reuse and renderer/geometry locality across hide/show. Inspector visibility alignment is a separate adapter and row-geometry regression.

tests.title: reorders a signal by drag-and-drop with row-position updates only
tests.primaryContract: Real Tree drag reorder changes canonical/frozen order and row positions while preserving stable waveform owner order/identity and causing no WaveDrom or local-geometry rebuild.
tests.reason: The companion Undo/Redo case verifies exact order restoration across surfaces but does not assert reorder's incremental rendering boundary; this case protects owner reuse and row-position-only invalidation.

tests.title: moves an arbitrary group as one semantic drag-and-drop operation
tests.primaryContract: Dragging the Payload Group above Control moves the group's complete stable Signal block as one semantic History operation without waveform/local-geometry rebuild.
tests.reason: This is the Cycle Left Tree group-reorder adapter and verifies the complete canonical block order plus one semantic commit. Transaction group drag tests exercise a different entity/domain owner and do not replace it.

tests.title: moves a signal across groups without changing its semantic role
tests.primaryContract: Moving a selected Signal into an otherwise empty Group through Bottom's Group dropdown preserves its stable identity and semantic role, updates the live current-group marker, and creates one reversible command.
tests.reason: signal-editor-group-dropdown.spec.ts moves a Signal into populated Payload; this case covers the empty Scratch Group destination, where membership projection and group visibility differ, while also asserting role/identity and History.

tests.title: restores exact Canonical/Left/Frozen/Timing row order and stable SVG identity through Undo and Redo of a reorder
tests.primaryContract: A signal reorder is undone/redone with exact Left/Frozen row order, unchanged Timing owner membership, stable SVG node identity, and correct History state.
tests.reason: This uniquely verifies history replay across Canonical-derived Left/Frozen order and Timing's deliberately stable owner set/SVG identity. The immediate reorder test covers incremental invalidation, not Undo/Redo projection convergence.

tests.title: cancels a drag preview without canonical or History changes
tests.primaryContract: Ending a signal reorder drag after establishing a drop preview cancels the preview, clears drop-position state, and leaves Canonical revision and History unchanged.
tests.reason: Committed reorder and Undo/Redo coverage do not exercise the pre-commit drag cancellation boundary; this is the only focused guard that a canceled preview is view-only and cannot create a semantic mutation.

tests.title: Signal Inspector exposes Reset Semantics, applies via the Semantic Command, and survives Undo/Redo
tests.primaryContract: Inspector Reset Semantics draft fields apply through the existing Semantic Command as one reversible change, and Undo/Redo resynchronizes the controls with Canonical state.
tests.reason: Command-layer reset validation does not cover the previously missing Inspector entry point, Draft-to-Apply gate, or the UI's Undo/Redo synchronization; this is the direct GUI contract for the #495 control surface.

tests.title: Reset source-time metadata follows Timeline insert and survives Save/Open
tests.primaryContract: Reset assert/deassert source-time metadata shifts with Timeline insertion, survives Undo/Redo, and persists through Save/Open without losing the semantic reset settings.
tests.reason: The reset lifecycle unit test covers timeline transform rules but not the combined Inspector-authored data, real Timeline command, history replay, and serialized document round trip.

tests.title: clipboard paste crosses the exact signal budget once and rejects overflow atomically
tests.primaryContract: Clipboard Paste can reach the exact signal cap once, then rejects the next Paste without changing revision/count/History and reports the resource-limit problem.
tests.reason: Shared boundary unit tests do not prove the Home clipboard adapter's result-aware behavior at the exact limit, including atomic rejection and user-visible Problems reporting.

tests.title: bulk registration crosses the exact signal budget once and rejects overflow atomically
tests.primaryContract: Bulk registration reaches the exact signal cap, then rejects an additional definition without changing the existing document or History and exposes the precise resource-limit error.
tests.reason: This exercises the Bulk Registration preview/apply adapter and exact-cap boundary; clipboard paste reaches the same limit through a different user-facing command path and cannot substitute for registration parsing/application.

tests.title: annotation import is rejected at the resource boundary without replacing the session
tests.primaryContract: An over-budget annotation file is rejected while preserving the pre-existing document, Annotation count, revision, and History, and the user receives a resource-limit diagnostic.
tests.reason: This protects the Annotation-specific import/replace session boundary with a valid existing annotation and exact resource-limit feedback; other file-import tests cover different parsers and entity caps.

tests.title: annotation import rejects deeply nested JSON before migration or replacement
tests.primaryContract: Deeply nested Annotation JSON is rejected by the bounded JSON parser before migration or document replacement, without changing Canonical revision.
tests.reason: The shared parser unit contract does not prove this file-input route invokes depth validation before Annotation migration; Signal Event Import has a separate parser adapter and remains independently covered.

tests.title: Signal Event Import rejects deeply nested JSON before values are replaced
tests.primaryContract: Deeply nested Signal Event JSON is rejected before replacing the selected Signal's values, leaving revision and History unchanged.
tests.reason: Signal Event Import previously bypassed the shared parse gate, so its adapter-specific ordering and no-replacement guarantee are distinct from Annotation import's depth check.

tests.title: Signal Event Import rejects an oversized file before it is read as JSON
tests.primaryContract: A file larger than the configured byte budget is rejected before JSON parsing and leaves Canonical revision and History unchanged.
tests.reason: Nesting-depth validation does not cover byte-size preflight; this uses an actual oversized file on disk because inline Playwright buffers have a 50MB cap, protecting the pre-read boundary itself.

tests.title: Advanced JSON rejects a resource overflow before document replacement
tests.primaryContract: Applying Advanced JSON with a cycle-count resource overflow reports validation failure before replacing the current document and leaves revision, History, Dirty, and session intact.
tests.reason: Advanced JSON is a separate whole-document replacement adapter and validates timeline cycle budget, unlike entity/file import routes; it specifically protects against replacing the active session on invalid JSON semantics.

tests.title: does not select an annotation rejected by import
tests.primaryContract: When Annotation import is rejected, the failed attempted Annotation is not selected and the previous selection remains unchanged.
tests.reason: The resource-limit suite protects document atomicity but this case isolates the success-only selection side effect after a rejected import; failed commands must not move transient selection to a nonexistent entity.

tests.title: does not select a transaction when creation is rejected
tests.primaryContract: When Transaction creation is rejected, no synthetic/nonexistent Transaction ID becomes selected and the prior selection remains unchanged.
tests.reason: Annotation import rejection covers a different create adapter/entity; this directly guards the Transaction create route's result-aware selection effect, which resource-budget tests alone do not assert.

tests.title: Review Refresh Checks is view-only
tests.primaryContract: Refreshing Review checks leaves Canonical revision, History, Dirty state, and render counters unchanged.
tests.reason: The review workflow filtering case proves filter/navigation are view-only after checks exist, but does not guard the explicit refresh action from mutating the document or triggering render work.

tests.title: Problems exposes Clear Filter for filter clearing
tests.primaryContract: Problems panel presents the Clear Filter affordance and no stale Refresh control in its current panel header.
tests.reason: This is a narrow panel-header/accessible-control migration guard: the full Review workflow case covers scope and severity filters but does not assert the Problems table's Clear Filter control or absence of the obsolete Refresh action. It verifies the affordance, not the clearing interaction itself.

tests.title: Review filters and navigates the shared Problems diagnostics without mutation
tests.primaryContract: Review scope/severity filters and Previous/Next navigation operate on shared diagnostics while preserving Canonical revision, History, and Dirty state.
tests.reason: This is the end-to-end diagnostics workflow across a real invalid edit, multiple scope/severity filter states, and navigation targets; refresh-only and layout-only tests cover separate boundaries and do not imply the workflow semantics.

tests.title: Check header separates Filter/Navigation/Summary/Status/Action into non-overlapping groups (#394)
tests.primaryContract: The five Check header groups remain in the intended order, share aligned control baselines, and do not overlap at the tested production viewport.
tests.reason: The behavioral Review workflow tests do not protect the #394 density regression where controls collide; this directly checks grouping, order, overlap, and alignment rather than duplicating filter behavior.

tests.title: Ribbon caption layout survives mode changes at 1280
tests.primaryContract: At 1280x720, changing Cycle/Transaction/Combined modes preserves Ribbon height and keeps each visible group caption below its body without pseudo-element duplication.
tests.reason: This compact viewport detects caption collision/wrapping changes during mode transitions that static Ribbon label tests do not measure; its paired wide case covers a distinct responsive width.

tests.title: Ribbon caption layout survives mode changes at 1672
tests.primaryContract: At 1672x941, changing Cycle/Transaction/Combined modes preserves Ribbon height and keeps each visible group caption below its body without pseudo-element duplication.
tests.reason: The reference-width counterpart checks group caption geometry over the same mode lifecycle; compact-width wrapping behavior cannot establish desktop alignment.

tests.title: Cursor A/B Ribbon controls set/swap/clear the status bar readout with zero Canonical/History delta
tests.primaryContract: View Ribbon controls set, move, swap, and clear source-time cursor A/B state, update guide/status projections, and remain view-only with zero History mutation.
tests.reason: This exercises the full Ribbon-to-workspace cursor lifecycle and status projection; geometry-only cursor tests do not cover set/swap/clear command wiring or no-History behavior.

tests.title: Cursor A guide drag updates only workspace cursor state
tests.primaryContract: Dragging Cursor A to a semantic Cycle boundary updates its source-time position while leaving Canonical and History unchanged.
tests.reason: The set/swap/clear case does not exercise pointer coordinate projection or guide drag; this separately protects the cursor-only drag mutation boundary.

tests.title: Home Ribbon labels and icons do not overlap at 1365px
tests.primaryContract: At 1365px, visible Home Ribbon icons and labels remain within their buttons and Timeline controls do not overlap neighboring controls, with no horizontal Ribbon overflow.
tests.reason: This intermediate-width overlap check targets icon/label and sibling-control geometry, not text wrapping alone; the 1672px case is its wide responsive counterpart and existing wrapping tests assert a different text contract.

tests.title: Home Ribbon labels and icons do not overlap at 1672px
tests.primaryContract: At 1672px, visible Home Ribbon icons and labels remain within their buttons and Timeline controls do not overlap neighboring controls, with no horizontal Ribbon overflow.
tests.reason: This verifies icon-label and Timeline sibling geometry at the approved wide reference width; the narrower viewport can fail independently, and word-boundary wrapping checks do not detect these collisions.

tests.title: does not create horizontal Ribbon overflow at 1024px
tests.primaryContract: At 1024px, the Home Ribbon's scroll width does not exceed its client width.
tests.reason: The 1024px responsive-overflow case already asserts the same no-scrollbar width invariant and additionally opens More to verify command reachability; retaining this standalone assertion duplicates that breakpoint.
tests.replacementTest: ribbon-responsive-overflow.spec.ts::keeps Home commands reachable without a Ribbon scrollbar at 1024px

tests.title: does not create horizontal Ribbon overflow at 1280px
tests.primaryContract: At 1280px, the Home Ribbon's scroll width does not exceed its client width.
tests.reason: The 1280px responsive-overflow case already asserts the same no-scrollbar width invariant and also verifies the major-group composition; this standalone width-only assertion is redundant at that breakpoint.
tests.replacementTest: ribbon-responsive-overflow.spec.ts::keeps Home commands reachable without a Ribbon scrollbar at 1280px

tests.title: does not create horizontal Ribbon overflow at 1672px
tests.primaryContract: At 1672px, the Home Ribbon's scroll width does not exceed its client width.
tests.reason: The responsive-overflow matrix does not exercise 1672px; this retains the standalone wide reference width as an independent overflow breakpoint.

tests.title: does not create horizontal Ribbon overflow at 900px
tests.primaryContract: At 900px, the Home Ribbon's scroll width does not exceed its client width.
tests.reason: 900px is a narrower overflow boundary than the 1024px menu-reachability case and independently catches failures below the compact breakpoint.

tests.title: keeps More popup inside the viewport and view-only at 1024px
tests.primaryContract: At 1024px, More popup stays inside viewport, supports arrow/Home/End focus navigation, closes on Escape or tab switch, restores focus, and causes no document mutation.
tests.reason: Command reachability at compact width does not cover popup geometry, menu keyboard contract, Escape focus restoration, tab-switch dismissal, or view-only lifecycle; this is the wider of two explicit compact corner checks.

tests.title: keeps More popup inside the viewport and view-only at 900px
tests.primaryContract: At 900px, More popup stays inside viewport, supports arrow/Home/End focus navigation, closes on Escape or tab switch, restores focus, and causes no document mutation.
tests.reason: This verifies the popup at the narrowest tested viewport where positioning and available menu space differ from 1024px; the command inventory test does not assert overlay bounds or keyboard dismissal lifecycle.

tests.title: keeps Home commands reachable without a Ribbon scrollbar at 1024px
tests.primaryContract: At 1024px, Home Ribbon has no horizontal scrollbar, relocates commands into More, exposes the required command set, and allows view-only Select All through that menu.
tests.reason: This is the compact-width command reachability contract and also absorbs the duplicate 1024px overflow-only assertion; no desktop grouping or standalone popup-bound test proves the relocated command inventory.

tests.title: keeps Home commands reachable without a Ribbon scrollbar at 1280px
tests.primaryContract: At 1280px, Home Ribbon remains scrollbar-free and exposes the documented major-group order; compact mode retains this contract while moving commands to More.
tests.reason: The 1280px boundary validates the full ribbon group composition while the paired 1024px case checks relocation/reachability; it also subsumes the standalone overflow-only assertion at the same width.

tests.title: Home overflow zoom presets remain view-only at compact width
tests.primaryContract: A zoom preset selected from the compact Home More menu changes view zoom while leaving Canonical revision, History, and Dirty state unchanged.
tests.reason: Menu reachability alone does not establish that a relocated zoom action uses the view-only route rather than mutating document/history state; this is a focused adapter contract.

tests.title: switches Ribbon tab content without touching Canonical, History, WaveDrom, RowLayout, geometry, or Inspector/Bottom state
tests.primaryContract: Switching Ribbon tabs preserves workspace position and does not change document or Inspector/Bottom visibility state.
tests.reason: Cross-tab state preservation is product behavior, but internal renderer counters and CSS group-class assertions make this too broad for routine PR; replace implementation-specific checks with observable state assertions.

tests.title: Insert tab creates a real canonical Signal through a SemanticCommand
tests.primaryContract: The Insert Ribbon action creates a Signal through the production command path and records one history mutation.
tests.reason: This verifies a Ribbon entry point reaches a canonical command and History, not only that the button is rendered.

tests.title: Review tab Problems button navigates to the Problems panel
tests.primaryContract: Activating Problems from the Review Ribbon exposes the Problems panel without document mutation.
tests.reason: A distinct navigation affordance with one direct user-visible assertion and low runtime.

tests.title: AI query previews and applies one scoped SemanticCommand
tests.primaryContract: The Ribbon AI route previews without mutation, validates locally, and applies one scoped rename as exactly one History unit.
tests.reason: The shared AI contract exists elsewhere, but this exercises the Ribbon-to-Bottom-panel entry route; retain only if this entry distinction remains intentional.

tests.title: AI preview cancellation leaves Canonical and History unchanged
tests.primaryContract: Canceling an AI preview preserves the canonical revision and History and leaves the selected target available.
tests.reason: Isolates the unique cancellation boundary; stale-revision behavior is covered by the fuller AI proposal workflow contract.

tests.title: Home Ribbon swaps Time/Layout for Transaction context on ViewMode change, with exact Undo/Redo and no canonical/history/dirty delta from the switch itself
tests.primaryContract: Switching between Cycle and Transaction changes the Home Ribbon group composition and Bottom context without mutating Canonical/History/Dirty; Transaction creation remains one Undo/Redo-able command.
tests.reason: Static responsive tests do not validate ViewMode-owned group projection or Bottom context synchronization, and the create/Undo/Redo portion protects the retained Transaction action route.

tests.title: Home Ribbon has no overlap/clipping in Transaction context at 1280x720
tests.primaryContract: At 1280x720 in Transaction context, the Home Ribbon scroll width does not exceed the client width.
tests.reason: The generic narrow Ribbon check runs without explicitly switching to Transaction context; this checks the different Transaction-context group set at the compact supported viewport.

tests.title: Home Ribbon has no overlap/clipping in Transaction context at 1672x941
tests.primaryContract: At 1672x941 in Transaction context, the Home Ribbon scroll width does not exceed the client width.
tests.reason: The wide reference check verifies overflow under Transaction-specific Home composition; Cycle/wide label geometry tests do not switch to this context or assert its client/scroll width relationship.

tests.title: captures deterministic production Ribbon scenario manifests
tests.primaryContract: At the reference viewport, each Ribbon tab produces a deterministic scenario manifest with icon/baseline diagnostics, capture metadata, and no console/page/resource failures.
tests.reason: This is the only all-tab production capture/manifest integrity sweep and validates the review-bundle evidence format as well as each tab's icon/baseline diagnostics; individual layout checks do not verify manifest completeness or runtime failures across all tabs.

tests.title: covers compressed Ribbon layout and Home round-trip without semantic mutation
tests.primaryContract: At 1365x800, Ribbon tab round-trips preserve Ribbon height/workspace position and document state, remain scrollbar-free, and yield clean compressed/round-trip icon-baseline manifests.
tests.reason: The desktop all-tab capture does not exercise the intermediate compressed viewport or repeated Home round-trip stability; this is a visual evidence scenario rather than routine semantic coverage.

tests.title: keeps the Ruler alive across edits, Undo/Redo, and repeated Opens with a non-default reference clock
tests.primaryContract: Ruler geometry remains present and correctly changes across Signal/event edits, Undo/Redo, and repeated opens of two documents with distinct non-default Reference Clock IDs and cycle counts.
tests.reason: Reference label persistence does not cover stale ruler/geometry ownership across successive document generations; this lifecycle specifically switches A→B→A and checks each document's tick projection after edits and history replay.

tests.title: derives the reference Clock label and edge from canonical state across Save/Open
tests.primaryContract: Selecting a different stable Reference Clock, changing its edge and name, and Save/Open derives the Time Axis status/context labels and serialized clock/edge from Canonical state.
tests.reason: The A→B→A ruler test only checks tick availability/count; this separately proves user-visible stable clock identity, edge, rename propagation, and persisted Time Axis ownership.

tests.title: the Ruler resolves and renders the terminal timeline boundary tick instead of silently omitting it
tests.primaryContract: For a half-open timeline [0, cycleCount), the Ruler resolves and renders the terminal cycleCount boundary at an X greater than the preceding tick.
tests.reason: Ordinary tick-count and reference-clock tests do not assert the final exclusive-end boundary, which may be represented only as the previous cycle's end geometry.

tests.title: Open then Annotation drag uses the current document geometry
tests.primaryContract: After opening a document, an Inspector-selected stable Annotation ID is used to drag its endpoint against the newly opened document's current Cycle geometry and snap to the intended cycle.
tests.reason: General Annotation drag tests do not exercise the Open→render-owner replacement→drag sequence; the target is now selected by Inspector's canonical Annotation ID rather than DOM order, preserving stable identity under overlay reuse.

tests.title: resize then edit then zoom reads current ViewMetrics and keeps semantics coherent
tests.primaryContract: After resizing Inspector, an immediate Signal edit and subsequent zoom use current ViewMetrics while preserving semantic selection/data and a mounted waveform.
tests.reason: The ordered resize→edit→zoom sequence catches stale layout metrics consumed by a later command; isolated resize and zoom cases cannot establish that consumers switch to the current metrics between operations.

tests.title: Signal Editor's in-progress Add/Edit Transition draft survives an unrelated canonical edit
tests.primaryContract: An uncommitted Bottom Signal event draft survives an unrelated canonical visibility edit to another Signal, retains the original editor selection, and is still explicitly cancelable.
tests.reason: Local field editing/Cancel tests do not protect against whole-document revision remount erasing the draft when another entity changes; this reproduces that cross-entity lifecycle directly.

tests.title: moves the selected Signal to a Group via the dropdown + Move button, using the real signal.move command
tests.primaryContract: Bottom's Group dropdown plus Move button invokes one reversible signal.move command, disables same-group no-op, and updates the selected Signal's current-group projection.
tests.reason: The sibling test covers moving into an empty Group; this covers the populated destination and same-group disabled guard through the dedicated Bottom editor adapter, preserving semantic role and Undo behavior.

tests.title: Inspector Signal Properties Apply stays disabled until the Draft actually differs from the committed Signal
tests.primaryContract: Inspector Apply is disabled for an unchanged Signal draft, becomes enabled after a role change without immediate Canonical mutation, then applies one update and disables again.
tests.reason: The broader Name/Role test validates independent commit paths, but this directly protects the Draft dirty-state gate and disabled/enabled transition that prevents accidental no-op Apply commands.

tests.title: Inspector applies per-signal vertical spacing through the canonical command
tests.primaryContract: Inspector spacing fields commit via the canonical Signal command, change the next row's rendered vertical position, avoid WaveDrom regeneration, and are Undoable.
tests.reason: This covers a layout-affecting Signal property and its actual row-geometry effect; role/name/type tests protect different property-specific rendering and command semantics.

tests.title: follows row selection and exposes derived Event Table columns
tests.primaryContract: The Bottom Signal editor follows the selected stable Signal and exposes its derived event rows with stable read-only Start/Value/End/Duration fields and quick-value actions.
tests.reason: Mutation tests assume an already selected Signal and do not assert selection-to-editor projection or the table's derived read-only columns; this is the base user entry/structure contract.

tests.title: commits one event edit once, rerenders only its waveform, and supports Undo
tests.primaryContract: Editing and saving one event changes that Signal's waveform exactly once, preserves unrelated waveform SVG identity and row positions, and Undo restores prior event semantics.
tests.reason: The simpler event-row tests establish editing UX but do not assert owner-local WaveDrom/geometry invalidation or that an unrelated waveform is retained; this is the direct incremental-render boundary.

tests.title: Inspector Name (Enter) and Role (Apply) each commit independently without WaveDrom regeneration
tests.primaryContract: Inspector name commits on Enter and role commits through Apply as two distinct one-revision actions, with the rendered row updated and WaveDrom untouched.
tests.reason: Apply gating covers only role-draft enablement and type/width covers a different command payload; this protects the separate InlineNameInput Enter commit and the intended independent Name/Role ownership paths.

tests.title: Inspector exposes editable type and bus width through one semantic command
tests.primaryContract: Inspector applies Signal type/role and Bus width together as one semantic command, and Undo restores the canonical width.
tests.reason: Bus width is type-specific canonical data and is not exercised by generic Name/Role/Spacing property cases; this verifies a single atomic type/width update and undo restoration.

tests.title: Bottom Signal event toolbar provides command-backed row operations, and the table footer provides export
tests.primaryContract: Bottom event toolbar exposes only Duplicate/Add Row/Delete, event export is available in the table footer, and Duplicate commits one additional row in one History unit.
tests.reason: This protects the post-#402 toolbar/footer ownership and a real row-duplicate command; import/undo, transition editing, and table selection are tested separately and do not assert the relocated export affordance.

tests.title: Bottom Signal event Import (table footer) replaces the table in one history entry and Undo restores it
tests.primaryContract: Importing an event table from the footer replaces the selected Signal's values in one History operation and Undo restores the prior table.
tests.reason: Resource-boundary tests protect rejected oversized/deep files, not successful replacement semantics, exact one-command history, or Undo restoration of the prior event table.

tests.title: edits Clock Generator through one semantic history entry
tests.primaryContract: Applying a Clock period edit produces one semantic History operation, regenerates only the Clock waveform/geometry owner once, and reflects the committed period in the editor.
tests.reason: Duty/suppressed-period cases cover specialized generator values; this is the base period-edit command and incremental owner invalidation contract.

tests.title: Bottom Clock editor applies exact non-50% Duty through WaveDrom and preserves Undo/Redo
tests.primaryContract: A 25% Clock duty edit changes the rendered WaveDrom use geometry, rebuilds only the clock owner once, and restores/reapplies through Undo/Redo and Save/Open.
tests.reason: Period editing does not validate non-50% duty rendering; this checks waveform geometry change, one-owner invalidation, history replay, and persisted duty semantics.

tests.title: Bottom Clock editor applies suppressed periods and preserves them through Save/Open
tests.primaryContract: Duplicate suppressed periods are rejected without History, valid distinct suppressed periods update the Clock waveform, and the accepted list survives Undo/Redo and Save/Open.
tests.reason: Duty/period tests do not cover suppression-list validation or phase omissions; this is the dedicated invalid/valid list boundary and persistence path.

tests.title: Bottom Clock editor exposes Edge Counter settings through its own semantic command
tests.primaryContract: Bottom Clock editor applies edge-counter visibility, edge mode, and count origin as one semantic operation, renders numbering without rebuilding WaveDrom/geometry, and Undo restores the disabled state.
tests.reason: Edge Counter is independent presentation metadata and has its own editor command; clock generator output edits do not verify numbering mode/count origin or overlay-only invalidation.

tests.title: Bottom Clock context toolbar exposes real preset, duplicate, import, export and preview actions
tests.primaryContract: The selected Clock context toolbar presents Presets/Duplicate/Import/Export/Preview, preview is view-only, the 50%-duty preset is actionable, and Duplicate creates/selects one Clock.
tests.reason: This protects the Clock-specific action surface and exercises preview/preset/duplicate behavior; Import and Export are asserted as available buttons here, not as completed file-I/O workflows, so dedicated file lifecycle tests remain necessary.

tests.title: moves the rendered waveform transition to the edited Start cycle, not just the DOM identity
tests.primaryContract: After editing an event Start cycle, the actual rendered transition geometry moves to the corresponding Ruler boundary while remaining absent from the old boundary.
