tests.reason: Canonical row-value assertions cannot establish that the WaveDrom transition moved to the new semantic cycle; this is the rendered geometry acceptance for Start editing.

tests.title: #402: Event row Save stays disabled until the Draft differs, and Cancel discards it back to canonical
tests.primaryContract: Read-only event rows expose no edit controls until Edit, unchanged Draft keeps Save disabled, changed Draft marks unapplied state, Cancel restores Canonical without History, and Save commits one operation.
tests.reason: Immediate Add semantics and unrelated-edit draft survival cover different workflows; this directly protects the row-local Edit→dirty draft→Cancel/Save lifecycle and avoids invisible idle inputs.

tests.title: Transitions table Select All is a real tri-state checkbox wired to the same selection the footer bulk actions use
tests.primaryContract: The transition table Select All checkbox correctly reflects unchecked/indeterminate/checked states, shares selection with per-row checkboxes and footer count, and honors bulk-action cardinality guards.
tests.reason: Transition reorder tests use selected rows but do not verify tri-state checkbox semantics, accessible row labels, selection count synchronization, or Delete/Move enablement constraints.

tests.title: Transition drag handle reorders rows through one history entry
tests.primaryContract: Dragging an individual transition handle changes event-row order through one semantic History operation and the updated row values are projected in order.
tests.reason: Selected block Move Up/Down actions are distinct toolbar command paths; neither protects the row drag-handle adapter and its one-operation commit.

tests.title: Selected transition block moves down as one semantic unit
tests.primaryContract: Moving a contiguous selected transition block down preserves block selection and performs one semantic reorder without creating or deleting rows.
tests.reason: This tests the direction-specific selected-block boundary and selection tracking; the up/Undo case covers the opposite edge and history replay, while drag reorder exercises another adapter.

tests.title: Selected transition block moves up and restores through Undo/Redo
tests.primaryContract: Moving a selected transition block upward changes its order once and Undo/Redo restores/reapplies the order while retaining the complete row set.
tests.reason: The selected-block down case does not cover upward boundary behavior or history replay; a drag-handle single-row move is not a substitute for selected contiguous-block movement.

tests.title: Signal event table explains its immediate-commit model and Add still produces one History entry
tests.primaryContract: The event form clearly communicates immediate per-Add commit semantics and adding an event creates exactly one History step.
tests.reason: The event Save/Cancel case covers deferred row-edit drafts, not the distinct immediate Add/Add & Continue interaction model; this pairs truthful guidance with its one-step behavior.

tests.title: shows an inset clear affordance only for non-empty signal filters
tests.primaryContract: The Signal Tree clear button appears only for non-empty input, is inset and vertically aligned within the search field, and clears the filter back to its absent state.
tests.reason: Filtering behavior tests do not protect the conditional clear affordance's containment/alignment or its empty-state disappearance; this is a compact UI geometry plus interaction contract.

tests.title: Generate Waveform computes a single pulse into the Signal's ordinary values, undoable and Save/Open-stable
tests.primaryContract: Generating a pulse writes ordinary Signal values in one undoable semantic operation and Save/Open preserves those values.
tests.reason: Covers canonical result, Undo/Redo, and a real file Save/Open cycle; retain as heavy integration rather than normal PR coverage.

tests.title: Generator supports an infinite periodic pulse train and suppressed periods, and rejects an invalid Width/Period without mutation
tests.primaryContract: Periodic generation honors suppressed periods, while an invalid width/period combination is rejected without Canonical or History mutation.
tests.reason: Combines a specialized periodic expansion with rejected-Apply safety; the table-driven arithmetic/validator portion should be moved to a cheaper layer where available.

tests.title: Duty mode computes Width from Period, and Generate Waveform is only offered for a Signal (binary), never Level/Bus/State/Event
tests.primaryContract: Duty configuration generates expected binary values and the generator action is absent for non-binary signal types.
tests.reason: Protects a distinct duty-mode conversion and type-capability boundary; retain one browser journey for UI gating, with arithmetic type cases covered in validator/unit tests.

tests.title: #402: Generate stays disabled once the computed Draft matches the Signal's current values
tests.primaryContract: When generator parameters produce the existing Signal values, the Generate action becomes unavailable and does not add another History entry.
tests.reason: This is a concise no-op protection against needless canonical mutation after the editor draft resets.

tests.title: Generator is secondary to the persistent Transition table and collapsing it preserves its draft
tests.primaryContract: Collapsing and reopening the secondary Generator disclosure preserves its unapplied values and leaves Canonical and History unchanged.
tests.reason: A short Draft lifecycle boundary distinct from Generate Apply; protects discoverability priority and non-destructive disclosure behavior.

tests.title: edits individual signal spacing through Inspector with local row invalidation and Save/Open
tests.primaryContract: Applying per-Signal spacing moves subsequent rows, updates row positions without WaveDrom/local-geometry rebuild, supports Undo/Redo, and survives Save/Open.
tests.reason: The base spacing case in signal-editor.spec.ts only checks a row displacement and Undo; this adds precise row-position-only invalidation plus persisted reconstruction for a Signal-specific spacing value.

tests.title: keeps invalid Group and Signal spacing drafts out of the canonical document
tests.primaryContract: Negative Group and Signal spacing drafts are rejected without Canonical revision, History, or Dirty changes.
tests.reason: Valid spacing persistence does not exercise invalid numeric values across both Group and Signal owners; this guards rejected drafts from leaking into Canonical state or creating History.

tests.title: edits Group and Signal spacing independently and together with exact persistence and export
tests.primaryContract: Group before/after spacing, Signal before/after spacing, and document layout spacing apply as separate commands, serialize exactly, restore through Save/Open, and remain represented in SVG/PNG/PDF exports.
tests.reason: This combines three distinct spacing owners and verifies exact file serialization plus all three export formats; local Signal spacing Save/Open alone cannot prove Group/global spacing ownership or export projection.

tests.title: Signal Split does not expose per-signal Upper/Lower/Both assignment
tests.primaryContract: Cycle Inspector does not expose the retired per-Signal Upper/Lower/Both Split Pane assignment control.
tests.reason: The existing Sample D dual-viewport acceptance already selects a Signal and asserts the retired Split Pane Inspector control is absent while exercising the canonical shared-row product model; this default-document absence-only check adds no distinct fixture or state transition.

tests.title: Signal Split shows the same canonical Signal sequence in both panes
tests.primaryContract: Both Split panes project the same first five canonical timing-row IDs in the default Cycle fixture.
tests.reason: The Sample D acceptance checks the complete 24-Signal canonical row sequence across both panes plus independent vertical/shared horizontal scroll and view-only behavior; its richer fixture subsumes this five-row prefix assertion.
tests.replacementTest: acceptance-397-sample-d.spec.ts::Signal Split ON shows the same 24-Signal row sequence in both panes with independent vertical scroll and shared horizontal scroll, OFF returns to one viewport, view-only throughout

tests.title: Signal Split remains view-only when a legacy assignment is present
tests.primaryContract: Retired per-Signal split assignment metadata/control must not affect the shared Split view; toggling Split remains view-only.
tests.reason: Despite its title, the test does not load legacy assignment data or assert Canonical/History/Dirty deltas; it only opens Split and checks that the Inspector field is absent. Sample D asserts the actual view-only ON/OFF flow and retired-control absence in the full shared-row model, so it supersedes this misleading default-fixture case.
tests.replacementTest: acceptance-397-sample-d.spec.ts::Signal Split ON shows the same 24-Signal row sequence in both panes with independent vertical scroll and shared horizontal scroll, OFF returns to one viewport, view-only throughout

tests.title: Signal Split is available only in Cycle View
tests.primaryContract: The Signal Split control is absent in Transaction and Combined modes and available in Cycle mode.
tests.reason: The Sample D shared-row acceptance runs in Cycle mode and does not prove mode gating; this directly protects availability boundaries across all three workspace modes.

tests.title: toggling Signal Split is view-only and Upper's own scroll position survives toggling Lower off and back on
tests.primaryContract: Toggling the Lower viewport is view-only and preserves Upper's horizontal scroll position across OFF/ON while the shared ruler remains synchronized.
tests.reason: Sample D covers dual-pane shared horizontal time and independent vertical scroll, but this additionally creates a nonzero Upper scroll position, removes/recreates Lower, and proves Upper's scroll survives that lifecycle.

tests.title: Upper and Lower scroll vertically independently while sharing one horizontal time domain
tests.primaryContract: Upper and Lower vertical scroll positions are independent while both rulers consume the same horizontal scroll and zoom domain.
tests.reason: Sample D verifies both panes' independently changing scroll positions and shared horizontal alignment with a 24-Signal fixture that provides real overflow; this short default-fixture test only moves Upper vertically and compares ruler transforms.

tests.title: Signal types stay synchronized through history and Save/Open at 1280x720
tests.primaryContract: The supported Signal type labels remain identical between creation and Inspector controls, and type changes survive Undo/Redo and Save/Open at 1280x720.
tests.reason: The compact viewport exercises the type-registry and persisted role contract under narrower responsive layout; the wide viewport cannot replace this breakpoint-sensitive check.

tests.title: Signal types stay synchronized through history and Save/Open at 1672x941
tests.primaryContract: The supported Signal type labels remain identical between creation and Inspector controls, and type changes survive Undo/Redo and Save/Open at 1672x941.
tests.reason: This proves the type-registry and serialized-role lifecycle at the wide acceptance viewport; the compact case independently protects the smaller layout.

tests.title: hiding a signal keeps its navigation row recoverable while removing its waveform row
tests.primaryContract: Hiding a Signal retains its navigation identity while removing it from timing/frozen/wave projections, and restoring it returns the same canonical Signal to aligned surfaces.
tests.reason: Stable SVG reuse tests cover renderer identity and Inspector tests cover row alignment; this protects the distinct user recovery path where a hidden item remains discoverable in the Tree and can be restored.

tests.title: creates a Spacer from the Insert Ribbon, duplicates/copies it, reorders it within its Group by drag, and rejects a cross-Group drop
tests.primaryContract: Insert, Duplicate, clipboard copy/paste, same-Group drag reorder, and cross-Group rejection preserve Spacer height/identity and semantic command/history rules.
tests.reason: This uniquely covers the Insert Ribbon adapter, fresh identity on copy, in-Group drag, and Core's cross-Group Spacer rejection; Tree Add and Group Inspector edit tests do not cover these operations.

tests.title: adds and edits a Spacer Row from the Group Inspector with Save/Open and Undo/Redo
tests.primaryContract: Group Inspector Spacer height drafts reject invalid values without commit, valid Apply commits one reversible edit, and height survives Save/Open and exports.
tests.reason: Tree Add covers creation and projection only; this covers Group Inspector height editing, invalid draft isolation, Apply, history, persistence, and export reconstruction.

tests.title: creates a first-class Spacer from the Tree Add surface
tests.primaryContract: Tree Add creates a canonical Spacer with one History entry and projects a row without rebuilding WaveDrom or local timing geometry.
tests.reason: Insert Ribbon and Group Inspector routes use different production adapters; this directly guards Tree Add selection, row projection, and the Spacer no-wave/no-geometry invalidation contract.

tests.title: Split active pane follows clicks on the Signal surface vs Transaction lanes, drives ActiveContext, and stays view-only
tests.primaryContract: In Combined mode, Signal-surface and Transaction-lane interactions update active-pane/ActiveContext ownership without Canonical or History mutation.
tests.reason: Sibling drag tests verify specific gesture routes; this covers general click/focus ownership, context-sensitive Ribbon change, and view-only behavior across both active panes.

tests.title: Cycle and Transaction restore their last valid Bottom tab independently
tests.primaryContract: Switching between Cycle and Transaction restores each mode's last valid Bottom tab without leaking the other mode's selection.
tests.reason: This is the only test of per-mode Bottom-tab memory and validates fallback to each mode's valid tab instead of a shared global selection.

tests.title: Combined routes a real Transaction bar drag to the Transaction pane only
tests.primaryContract: A real Transaction bar drag in Combined mode mutates the Transaction through its owner, leaves Cycle editor idle, and activates the Transaction pane.
tests.reason: This real-pointer Transaction gesture asserts one semantic edit, Cycle editor isolation, and active-pane ownership; Signal range selection and mode-switch tests do not replace it.

tests.title: Transaction to Combined and back preserves Transaction ownership
tests.primaryContract: Transaction remains the active owner on entering Combined and its bars remain present after returning to Transaction, with no new History entry.
tests.reason: Active-pane interaction does not cover mode transition restoration; this checks Transaction→Combined→Transaction ownership and view-only History preservation.

tests.title: Combined routes a Signal waveform range drag to the Signal pane only
tests.primaryContract: A real waveform range drag in Combined resolves source cycles from Cycle ruler geometry, routes selection to the Signal pane, and creates no Canonical/History change.
tests.reason: Transaction drag protects the opposite owner route; this specifically verifies Signal range coordinates/source cycles and view-only selection in Combined.

tests.title: low-level view mode pointerdown cancels a Transaction drag before pointerup
tests.primaryContract: A low-level mode switch during an active Transaction drag cancels the preview before pointerup and prevents a stale semantic edit from committing.
tests.reason: Completed drag and mode round-trip tests do not exercise cancellation during an in-flight pointer sequence; this guards against stale gesture ownership committing after workspace change.

tests.title: never generates a colliding Stable ID after a page reload resets the in-memory counter
tests.primaryContract: After Save/Open in a fresh module session resets the in-memory ID counter, newly created Signals still receive IDs unique across the document.
tests.reason: Stable IDs are canonical identity rather than position; this exercises actual restore and subsequent authoring that can expose counter collisions beyond pure generator unit tests.

tests.title: reorders row shells without rerendering or moving heavy WaveDrom SVG owners
tests.primaryContract: Row-shell reorder and viewport remount preserve heavy WaveDrom SVG owner identity/order while only updating row positions and keeping canonical/rendered row mappings aligned.
tests.reason: This deterministic Phase 5 surface probe measures expensive SVG owner identity and render counters across viewport remount/reorder; product-level reorder tests do not enforce renderer reuse.

tests.title: reflects workspace, view mode and zoom without mutation
tests.primaryContract: Status context, mode status and zoom status reflect user changes to workspace preset, active Cycle mode and zoom while Canonical revision, History depth and Dirty status stay unchanged.
tests.reason: This is the only combined status-readout journey for workspace preset and zoom changes with explicit Canonical/History/Dirty invariants; a lower-level test cannot prove that the visible status widgets follow the user-facing controls. The title is limited to the state actually exercised (selection scope is covered separately in the next case).

tests.title: titlebar view-title always agrees with the status bar's Mode (#199)
tests.primaryContract: The titlebar view title and status-bar mode label agree across Cycle, Transaction and Combined mode switches without changing Canonical revision, History depth or Dirty status.
tests.reason: This is a distinct cross-mode naming parity contract; the workspace/zoom status test does not switch through the three mode-title pairs.

tests.title: exposes Bottom pin/follow state and selected hierarchy scope
tests.primaryContract: Status context exposes the selected hierarchy scope and reflects Bottom Follow versus Fixed and Pinned state after the corresponding user controls change without changing Canonical revision, History depth or Dirty status.
tests.reason: Selection-scope status and the two independent Bottom positioning controls are not covered by workspace/zoom mode status or by Bottom layout tests; this concise UI journey verifies their visible readout and view-only invariant.

tests.title: exposes and clears a temporary arrow-pick mode
tests.primaryContract: Starting endpoint-pick mode announces its temporary active step in the tool-status area, and Escape returns that visible status to the normal Select tool without changing Canonical revision, History depth or Dirty status.
tests.reason: Other arrow tests verify endpoint selection and annotation creation, but this is the direct visible contract for temporary tool status, its Escape reset and view-only lifecycle.

tests.title: multiple TimeGroups keep stable IDs, axis-break markers, history, and Save/Open semantics
tests.primaryContract: Two independently-created TimeGroups retain stable IDs and presentation metadata through collapse/expand history, actual Save/Open, and ruler marker projection.
tests.reason: The single lifecycle covers multi-entity identity, editing, collapse-marker projection, one-step Undo/Redo, serialization, and production Open. This persistence integration contract is not established by isolated mapping tests; keep it in integration rather than the routine PR path.

tests.title: production browser mapping path records 100k-cycle 0-fold and 1k-fold scale evidence
tests.primaryContract: The production browser mapping path processes 100k source cycles with zero and 1k collapsed folds while reporting bounded build/cache counters and attaching reproducible scale evidence.
tests.reason: This is a large production-path scaling measurement, not routine functional coverage. Its 100k-cycle replacements and 120-second waits make it inappropriate for frequent PR execution; unit benchmarks complement but do not replace browser integration overhead and session counters. Runtime has not been measured in this review.

tests.title: selects a cycle from Canvas geometry and the exclusive terminal boundary from shared mapping
tests.primaryContract: A waveform-positioned click selects its ruler-derived source cycle, while the shared mapping's exclusive terminal boundary remains selectable after horizontal reveal, with no semantic mutation.
tests.reason: This couples visible waveform coordinates to cycle selection and separately exercises navigation to the true terminal boundary in a compact, explicit fixture. It complements rendered-waveform boundary coverage by verifying the source mapping and read-only status invariant.

tests.title: keeps ruler click suppression scoped to ruler-originated gestures
tests.primaryContract: Waveform click/drag and ruler click/drag remain distinguishable; suppression of a synthetic post-drag click is scoped to the originating surface and does not swallow the next intentional gesture.
tests.reason: The journey protects cross-surface gesture ownership and stale click-suppression lifecycle. Unit-level pointer conversion cannot establish that subsequent user gestures on the other surface remain available.

tests.title: selects Cycle 0 and the terminal boundary from the rendered waveform
tests.primaryContract: Clicks at waveform geometry corresponding to Cycle 0 and the revealed exclusive terminal boundary select the correct half-open cells without changing Canonical, History, or Dirty state.
tests.reason: Although it shares terminal-boundary coverage with the mapping/ruler case, this exercises the rendered waveform hit-testing surface and specifically Cycle 0 at the left edge; the sibling verifies ruler-derived source mapping. Retain both surface contracts.

tests.title: selects a half-open range directly on the geometry-derived ruler
tests.primaryContract: A normal ruler click selects one cycle and Shift-click extends to the expected half-open source-cycle range, with exactly those cycle cells marked selected and no Canonical mutation.
tests.reason: This is the only Shift-click extension contract for the ruler. Drag-selection tests cover pointer-drag semantics and preview lifecycle, not modifier-click anchoring or selected-cell count.

tests.title: drag-selects a half-open Canvas range with preview-only movement and Escape cancel
tests.primaryContract: Waveform drag creates a preview-only half-open range, Shift-drag extends the existing range, and Escape cancels an active drag while Canonical, History, Dirty, and renderer counters remain unchanged.
tests.reason: The test protects the waveform-specific preview/commit/cancel lifecycle and guards renderer work during pointer movement. Ruler drag siblings do not prove this surface's routing or Shift extension behavior.

tests.title: positions a transaction ending at cycleCount on the actual terminal ruler geometry
tests.primaryContract: A newly-created Transaction whose end equals timeline cycleCount has a rendered right edge aligned within one pixel of the actual terminal ruler boundary.
tests.reason: This specifically verifies end-exclusive Transaction projection at the un-folded terminal boundary. The folded TimeGroup sibling verifies shared mapping alignment at an interior fold boundary, so neither subsumes the other.

tests.title: keeps transaction source-cycle edges aligned after a collapsed TimeGroup
tests.primaryContract: A Transaction ending at a collapsed TimeGroup boundary projects its right edge to the same screen X as the source-cycle ruler tick after switching from Cycle to Transaction.
tests.reason: This is the cross-mode folded-axis counterpart to the uncollapsed terminal-edge case; it proves Transaction consumes shared DisplayTimeMapping at a TimeGroup boundary despite mode-specific frozen-column origins.

tests.title: drag-selects a geometry-backed half-open range directly on the cycle ruler
tests.primaryContract: Ruler drag selects the same half-open source range in either drag direction, reaches the exclusive terminal boundary, preserves the prior committed selection on Escape, and permits a later drag to replace it.
tests.reason: The sibling waveform drag covers another surface; this adds reverse-direction normalization, ruler terminal-boundary dragging, and Escape-then-retry lifecycle that the simpler Shift-click contract does not exercise.

tests.title: ruler range drag cancels without mutation and remains semantic after scroll and zoom
tests.primaryContract: A pointer-cancelled ruler drag leaves the existing range intact; subsequent ruler drags after horizontal scroll and zoom resolve the intended source-cycle intervals.
tests.reason: This uniquely exercises pointercancel plus semantic coordinate resolution after two view transforms. It complements the direct ruler drag's reverse/terminal/Escape cases; no broad suite is required for this static classification.

tests.title: inserts cycles with full semantic ripple and one Undo entry
tests.primaryContract: Inserting cycles shifts signal events and the period-one Clock's generated source semantics together, publishes one semantic/history operation, and regenerates the expected visible WaveDrom and local geometry owners; Undo restores prior event positions.
tests.reason: The default-clock insertion smoke checks only that insertion succeeds and length/history change. This explicit period-one fixture validates event ripple and renderer invalidation counts, so it protects a distinct semantic+incremental-consumer contract.

tests.title: allows ordinary timeline insertion with the default uncontrolled periodic Clock
tests.primaryContract: The ordinary uncontrolled default Clock permits a half-open range insertion through the production Timeline editor and produces one canonical/history change with the expected cycle count.
tests.reason: The broader transform matrix repeats insertion as its first operation, but this isolated short PR smoke gives direct low-cost feedback for the common insertion path without requiring the four-operation matrix to run.

tests.title: allows all ordinary timeline transforms with the default uncontrolled periodic Clock
tests.primaryContract: Insert, delete, duplicate, and move through the ordinary Timeline UI each produce one semantic/history operation and the expected resulting timeline length with an uncontrolled periodic Clock.
tests.reason: The matrix covers the four user-facing transform commands against the ordinary default Clock. Its repeated fresh-page setup is more expensive than the dedicated insertion smoke, but each operation protects a separate adapter/command route.

tests.title: moves an uncontrolled Clock generator start with its source-time range
tests.primaryContract: Moving a source-time range also moves the uncontrolled Clock generator start, and Undo/Redo restore/apply the matching generator start.
tests.reason: The ordinary transform matrix checks resulting timeline lengths but does not inspect Clock generator metadata. This directly guards source-time generator ripple and its reversible history behavior.

tests.title: preserves a timeline transform exactly through Save/Open
tests.primaryContract: A committed timeline insertion survives Save, New, and production Recent/Open with the resulting cycle count and shifted Signal events intact, while the reopened document starts with clean History.
tests.reason: This complements the Clock move Undo/Redo test with serialization and restore of transformed Signal data. Neither an in-memory command test nor the TimeGroup-specific persistence case proves this timeline-edit Save/Open route.

tests.title: deletes a half-open range and preserves the active value at the join
tests.primaryContract: Deleting a half-open interval preserves the active value at the join, updates terminal ruler geometry and renderer consumers, and is represented by one undoable semantic operation.
